question: Compounds containing dry ice, mothballs, iodine crystals, and zinc change directly from solid to gaseous state by which of the following methods without going into the liquid state?
solution:
The correct answer is **__sublimation__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Sublimation**

__
 
• Sublimation is a physical change where **substances directly change from solid to gas without passing through a liquid state.**
 
• When a substance is heated from the solid state, it does not acquire the liquid state, but directly changes into the gaseous state, and on cooling again, it does not change from the gaseous state to the liquid state and directly into the solid state, this is called sublimation.
 
• The major examples of sublimation are **iodine, camphor, naphthalene, ammonium chloride, solid carbon dioxide, etc.**
 
• By this method camphor, naphthalene, ammonium chloride, anthracene, benzoic acid etc. **substances are purified.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evaporation**

 
 
• Evaporation is the process in which **an element or compound changes into a gas state**.
 
• In chemistry, the process of change from liquid to vapor is called **'evaporation'.**
 
• There are two types of evaporation- evaporation and boiling.
 
 
 
• **Condensation**
 
 
• Condensation is the process in which **atmospheric water vapor changes into water or ice particles.**
 
• It is the exact **opposite process of evaporation**.
 
• When the temperature of a saturated air falls below the dew point, that air cannot hold as much moisture inside it as it previously held.
 
• Therefore, the excess amount of moisture gets converted into tiny water droplets or ice particles according to the temperature.
 
 
 
• **Melting**
 
 
• Melting is the physical process in which **a solid substance changes into a liquid phase.**
 
• The **melting point **of a solid is the temperature at which it melts from its solid state to a liquid state.
 
• The solid and liquid phases are in equilibrium at the melting point.
